alignments.note: Postpositive γάρ takes the ASV's clause-initial *for*.
Ordinary negative οὐκ → *not*; no negative indefinite stands with it, so rules 41 and 59 are not in question.
Inflected verb takes its supplied subject and modal auxiliary under rules 7 and 9, headed on the lexical verb *endure* rather than on *they* or *could*, per rules 9 and 17.

Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun and nothing else, so it keeps *that* while the relativizer and copula ride with the participle. Rule 90 would apply only if the ASV had written a single word for the pair; it writes two.
Attributive participle rendered as a finite relative clause: *which* and *was* are rule 7 and 9 helpers on the participle, headed on the lexical *enjoined* under rule 17.

Crasis κἄν (καί + ἐάν) is one source word spelling a conjunction and a conditional particle, so it takes both English words as one aligned unit under rule 55. Rule 55 heads a crasis on the pronominal element; here the non-καί element is the conditional, so the head is *If*, the word introducing the clause under rule 40. Heading on *even* is the competing reading, but rule 82 refuses a head on *even* where another word realizes the clause-introducing element.
Anarthrous noun with a supplied indefinite determiner: rule 51's anarthrous clause makes *a* an ordinary rule 7 helper on the noun.
Aorist subjunctive rendered by the bare English verb.
Article surfaces as English *the* under rule 19; the genitive here takes no *of* in the ASV's phrasing, so nothing else rides with it.
Noun stands alone, its determiner having gone to the article under rule 21.
Future passive takes its supplied subject and both auxiliaries under rules 7 and 9, headed on the lexical participle *stoned* rather than on *shall* or *be*, per rules 9 and 17.

review_notes: All 11 source and all 20 target ids partitioned exactly once; no unrepresented or added units in this verse.

The article s004 is the only contested unit: rule 32 splits it from the participle, giving it *that* alone. Rule 90's single-word relaxation does not apply because the ASV writes *that which*, two words.

κἄν is treated as a crasis under rule 55 rather than as a rule 39 noncompositional particle cluster, since rule 39 is scoped to a particle fused with the negative μή and both English words here answer to source elements.
